name: OlegDB
tagline: Tongue-in-cheek but working C/Go key-value store: mmap hash table, LZ4, splay-tree cursors and a REST API.
description: OlegDB is a small key-value datastore that began in 2014 as a joke about NoSQL marketing (its consistency model is 'MAYO') but is real, working software. The core is a C library, liboleg, implementing a concurrent hash table keyed with MurmurHash3, an optional splay tree for ordered cursor iteration and prefix matching, LZ4 value compression, key expiry, a memory-mapped values file and an append-only log for persistence that can be compacted; a Go server puts an HTTP interface in front of it, and the library can be embedded directly. The last tagged release is 0.1.7 (April 2020), with a single compile fix pushed in October 2025. Fun to read and hack on; not something to bet a product on.
statusNote: No feature work since the 0.1.7 tag (April 2020); only an occasional build fix (October 2025).
strengths: Small, well-documented C codebase that is pleasant to read
Ordered iteration and prefix matching via splay trees
weaknesses: Hobby project with no active development
useCases: Learning how hash-table key-value stores work
Toy or hobby services needing a REST KV store
notIdealFor: Anything needing security or high availability
